rows.note: Session 646-9day2 did not reach 32 distinct end nodes, so its exploration efficiency was undefined and was set to zero in the comparisons with simulations (ED Fig. 2f,i). Mouse 1616's two special return sessions were included in the pooled return analyses of ED Fig. 2.

rows.analysis: PV, place map, level map and ensemble rate correlations across session intervals
Neural correlations across successive recording cycles
rows.note: All 14 mice contributed 37 pairs, including the special 14-day pair from mouse 1616; cycle-based analyses do not use the fixed-month exclusion.

rows.analysis: Reward location decoding and PV correlation, and neural-behavior associations
rows.panels: Fig. 4d,f; ED Fig. 8a to c; ED Fig. 10a,b
rows.note: Day i sources with reward experience gave 30 pairs from 14 mice. Six pairs (422day1, 837day1, 838day1, 839day1, 842day1 and 862day1, each to its 3-month session) were omitted because their Day i source was a latent day1 session in which no water was available. ED Fig. 8b,c also used Day i+1 sources (36 pairs). In ED Fig. 8b,c, a location was included only if it had at least 20 retained frames in both sessions, to avoid decoding errors and population vectors estimated from very few frames; there was no minimum number of visits. In two Day i+1 pairs (451-6day2 to 451-9day1 and 468day2 to 468-3day1), one of the three control locations did not meet this criterion, and the comparison used the other two.

rows.analysis: Standardized route PV correlation, second-day comparisons and equal-frame controls
rows.note: Route analyses used the 30 pairs with a rewarded Day i source. A pair entered a direction only if both sessions had at least five complete traversals in that direction. Home to reward excluded 434day1 to 434-3day1 (3 traversals in 434-3day1) and 468day1 to 468-3day1 (2 in 468day1). Reward to home excluded 468day1 to 468-3day1 (1 in 468day1), and 451day1 to 451-3day1 and 451-3day1 to 451-6day1 (4 in 451-3day1). The second-day comparison repeated the included pairs one day later and therefore omitted the same pairs; every Day i+1 session had at least five traversals. The equal-frame control used the same pairs.

rows.analysis: Standardized PV correlation along node 2 and node 3 routes
rows.note: Node routes used the same 30 pairs and the same five-traversal rule. Node 2 routes kept all 30 pairs in both directions. Node 3 routes excluded 418day1 to 418-3day1 in both directions (3 node 3 to reward and 2 reward to node 3 traversals in 418day1).

rows.analysis: Standardized route PV correlation relative to within-day reliability
rows.note: Pairs as in Fig. 4e. Each pair contributed an across-gap correlation and two within-day correlations, one per session, each between that session's odd and even runs. These were first averaged within each mouse, and the mouse's across-gap mean was then divided by the geometric mean of its two within-day means. A mouse was included only if both its reward and its elsewhere values could be adjusted. Mouse 434 had no home to reward pair. Its only reward to home pair, 434day1 to 434-3day1, could not be adjusted. In 434-3day1 the mouse made only five reward to home runs, and its odd and even runs did not agree at the reward bin (correlation −0.02). A geometric mean of a positive and a negative correlation does not exist, so mouse 434 has no adjusted value. The panel therefore includes 13 mice in each direction, with 28 home to reward pairs and 26 reward to home pairs.

rows.analysis: Standardized route PV correlation between approach and departure
rows.note: Only pairs included in both directions were used. These are the 30 pairs above without 468day1 to 468-3day1 (excluded in both directions), 434day1 to 434-3day1 (no home to reward) and 451day1 to 451-3day1 and 451-3day1 to 451-6day1 (no reward to home), leaving 26 pairs from 13 mice. The same matched neurons contributed to all curves.

rows.analysis: Recurrence of neural correlations across consecutive long gaps
rows.note: Consecutive-gap recurrence requires three eligible successive cycles. Mice 434, 579 and 1616 lacked three eligible long-gap cycles, but remained in single-gap analyses; the short-gap 1616 chain was excluded.

rows.analysis: Within-session convergence, early alignment and local stability
rows.panels: Fig. 3e,f,h,i,k,l; ED Fig. 6c to h; ED Fig. 9m,n
rows.note: All 59 Day i/Day i+1 pairs from the 22 mice were used; none was excluded.

rows.analysis: Age and early within-cycle neural correlations
Port advantage on rewarded and timeout approaches
rows.note: This comparison needed at least five rewarded and five timeout home to reward approaches in both sessions of a pair. Of the 36 long-gap pairs, 25 pairs from 12 mice qualified. The six pairs whose Day i source was a latent day1 session were excluded because that session had no rewarded approaches (422day1, 837day1, 838day1, 839day1, 842day1 and 862day1, each paired with its 3-month session). Five other pairs had too few approaches of one outcome. 434day1 to 434-3day1 was excluded because 434-3day1 had 3 rewarded and no timeout approaches. 468day1 to 468-3day1 was excluded because 468day1 had 2 rewarded and no timeout approaches and 468-3day1 had 1 timeout approach. 468-3day1 to 468-6day1 was excluded because 468-3day1 had 1 timeout approach. 422-3day1 to 422-6day1 was excluded because 422-6day1 had 4 timeout approaches. 488-3day1 to 488-6day1 was excluded because 488-6day1 had 4 rewarded approaches. Mice 422 and 434 therefore had no eligible pair.
